title: Refit a loaded drawer on its roller slides, carried in above riding height so the rear hooks clear, then pull-test it
instruction: Put the drawer back into the cabinet on its slides and close it. Then pull it open again by about 5 cm and leave it there.
context: Cabinet fitters and movers refit drawers after a repair or a move. On roller slides a hook under the rear half of each drawer runner must pass over the rail's front roller, so the loaded drawer has to be carried in level, slightly above riding height, until the hooks are past the rollers, then set down. A wrong fit is hidden: pushed in low, the drawer slides along the cabinet floor under the slides and still closes flush. Only a pull test shows it: on its slides the drawer runs out level and stops at its hooks; under the slides it sits 54 mm lower, drags out with no stop. Unlike removing a drawer by holding its two slide releases pressed while pulling, this tests engaging a hidden catch by controlling the insertion height of a loaded drawer, a fault that looks right when closed. Unlike lifting a drawer's front to take it out past its anti-pull-out stop, or stowing a console drawer that already rides on its rails, the slides start disengaged; opening the drawer is only the check.
setup: World frame in metres: x forward from the arms, y left, z up; the table top is z = 0.7475 and the arm bases are at x 0, y +/-0.305. Cabinet (fixed, wood): 40 cm wide, 26 cm deep, 17 cm tall, open at the top, its front face at x = 0.32 centred on y = 0; 12 mm floor panel, 18 mm side walls and back. Inside each side wall a steel slide rail 22 mm wide, 12 mm thick, 235 mm long, its top 90 mm above the table, with a steel front roller (8 mm long, 6 mm high) 2 mm behind the face. Drawer (free, 1.0 kg): painted front panel 390 x 18 x 100 mm, plywood box 300 mm wide, 202 mm deep, 90 mm tall with 12 mm walls and a 10 mm bottom; on each side a steel runner 197 x 22 x 12 mm, 30 mm above the drawer bottom, and under the rear half of each runner a 112 mm long, 6 mm thick orange hook plate whose front end is the rear hook. On its slides the drawer bottom is 66 mm above the table; it opens 75 mm before the hooks meet the rollers. Pushed in low it rests on the cabinet floor 12 mm above the table with its runners passing under the rails. At the start the drawer stands on the table with its front panel's outer face at x = 0.06, centred on y = 0, holding a blue box of parts (120 x 160 x 60 mm, 0.8 kg) centred 145 mm behind the front face. Friction: runners, hook plates, rails and rollers 0.05 (standing in for rolling); drawer wood 0.8; cabinet wood 0.5; parts box 1.2.
scoring: Judged from the video and a photo of the end with a ruler. On its slides means: the drawer bottom 66 +/- 4 mm above the table (both runners riding on the rails, measured at the front panel), level within 2.5 degrees, square to the cabinet within 3 degrees and centred within 12 mm, and open no more than 78 mm (it stops at 75 mm when the hooks meet the rollers). Closed means the front panel within 5 mm of the cabinet face. Hands off means both grippers at least 2 cm from the drawer and the box. Score 0 if the box ever leaves the drawer or the drawer falls off the table. Otherwise 1.0 if, after the drawer was closed on its slides with hands off for 1 s, it is now on its slides, open 30 to 80 mm, the box inside, hands off (the trial ends as a success once this has held for 1 s); 0.5 if it was closed on its slides with hands off for 1 s and is still on its slides; 0.25 if it is on its slides; else 0. The state at the end of the episode is scored.
reset_notes: Take the drawer out, stand it on its marks on the table with the box in it, and clear the closed-and-let-go record. There is one fixed layout; the episode seed does not change the scene.
fidelity: Rigid boxes. Roller slides are modelled as low-friction (0.05) sliding contacts with a fixed 6 mm roller step at the front of each rail; no self-closing spring or damper. Sizes are real scale for a small desk or bedside drawer unit (300 mm wide drawer box), but the drawer is 202 mm deep, shallower than a 450 mm kitchen drawer, to stay within the arms' reach. The 1.0 kg drawer and 0.8 kg load are realistic for that size, lighter than a full kitchen drawer.
